title: Senate cuts P19.8B from AICS, MAP budget, reallocates to PhilHealth subsidy
summary: The Senate has slashed nearly P20 billion from the allocated budget for the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) and the Medical Assistance Program (MAP) under the proposed 2027…

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 4:36pm

The Senate has slashed nearly P20 billion from the allocated budget for the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) and the Medical Assistance Program (MAP) under the proposed 2027 national budget.

Senate Finance panel chairman JV Ejercito announced this Wednesday, noting that the financial assistance programs each suffered a P9.9 billion reduction — which will be reallocated to Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) subsidy.

With P19.8 billion reallocated, Ejercito said the budget for PhilHealth subsidy now stands at P94.2 billion, up from P73 billion initially allocated under the House-approved General Appropriations Bill (GAB).
“Ang ayuda, partly ... we will partly slash and nilagay namin ‘yung marami sa PhilHealth. Kaya Philhealth, sa subsidy will increase by almost P20 billion,” he said in an ambush interview.
(We will partially reduce the financial assistance and reallocate a significant portion to PhilHealth. The subsidy under PhilHealth will increase by nearly P20 billion.)

“P74 billion, P73 billion, magiging P94 [billion]. Ang target nga natin gawing P100 billion pero masikip ang fiscal space. So hopefully kung maabot ‘yung P100 billion para mas maganda ang subsidy ng PhilHealth,” he added.

(From P74 billion or P73 billion, it will become P94 billion. Our target was actually to reach P100 billion, but fiscal space is tight. Hopefully, we can reach that P100 billion allocation to provide a better subsidy under PhilHealth.)

The Senate Finance panel chair said that with higher subsidies for PhilHealth, there will be an increased budget for the zero balance billing, preventive care, immunization and health promotion, and for the health facilities enhancement program to improve provincial hospitals and locally funded health facilities.
“Lahat sa healthcare saka sa infrastructure, that is our priority,” Ejercito said.
(Everything related to healthcare and infrastructure, that is our priority.)
'Double funding'
Ejercito likewise committed that alleged duplicate funding for some projects will be rechecked and will be corrected if verified.
“Definitely, kapag may red flag at mga double entry, tanggal kaagad ‘yun. Syempre…humanly impossible mache-check mo, libo ‘yan. Dahan dahan, kaya nga iniisa-isa namin,” he said.

(Definitely, if there’s a red flag or a double entry, it’s removed immediately. Of course… it’s humanly impossible to check everything—there are thousands of items. We’re taking it step by step, slowly.)
“Siguro may nakakalusot. Kung may nakakalusot man, talagaang ano ‘yun, unintentional,” he added.
(It’s possible that some irregularities slipped through. If any did, it’s truly unintentional.)
Ejercito said he is seeking help from budget watchdogs and the public to help monitor any questionable items in the proposed 2027 national budget.

Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson earlier flagged duplicate appropriations for some flood control projects in the proposed 2027 national budget, raising fresh concerns over funding irregularities amid the ongoing controversy over anomalous flood control projects.
Lacson said the duplicate allocations were separate from at least 30 alleged ghost multipurpose buildings (MPBs) his team had identified in the proposed budget.

Lacson had also questioned the proposed appropriations for 3,950 MPBs, separate from the 1,584 MPBs covered by the Local Government Support Fund's (LGSF) Financial Assistance to local government units (LGUs) subprogram from 2022 to 2026. — RSJ, GMA News
